purpose: Teach: しだい/顔つき/過ぎ去っ/おねがい/ちがっ/あらわし/気が付く/どきどき

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「お便り届きしだい」と仰ってたぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when your father was young, he used to say letters arrived when they were meant to.
lines.style: Gentle, distant voice. Pause before each memory surfaces. Slow, careful pacing. The tone of someone holding something precious and fragile in their hands across decades.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃんの顔つきは、いつも穏やかでいらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mm, his face was always so peaceful, wasn't it? Don't you think so?
lines.style: Warm, conversational drawl. Slight rise at the end — genuinely curious for his agreement. The easy intimacy of someone who can ask without needing the answer.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと若い時代は過ぎ去ってしまったぞ
lines.en: Gran, those days with your father, those young years — they've slipped away from us.
lines.style: Voice catches slightly on the realization. Slower than before. Weight in the middle words. Trailing off as if the thought is too large to hold.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、孫から「おねがい」とお願いされてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, the grandchildren used to ask him for things, didn't they? Don't you remember?
lines.style: Softer, almost coaxing — drawing him back to the happy details. Gentle insistence, like turning a page in a book they both know by heart.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんのお考えとちがって、私は反対したぞ
lines.en: Gran, I was different from him. When it came to that, I opposed it.
lines.style: Firmer than the wistfulness before. A note of something harder — old disagreement surfacing. Then softens again, accepting it was his choice to make.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ご自分のお気持ちを書道であらわしていらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He used to express his feelings through calligraphy, didn't he? Those beautiful brushstrokes.
lines.style: Wonder in the voice — seeing it again across time. Slower pace. Touches on each word with reverence. Lingering on the image like she can still see the ink on the paper.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さんは細かい事にも気が付く方だったぞ
lines.en: Gran, he was the kind of man who noticed everything — even the smallest details.
lines.style: Quiet pride mixed with sadness. Speaking about him like he's present in the room. Steady, deliberate. The voice of someone counting his qualities like a inventory of the heart.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様にお会いになる時、どきどきされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: When he would see the grandchildren, his heart would race with joy, wouldn't it? I could see it in him.
lines.style: Warmth breaking through. Voice softens into genuine tenderness. A small, knowing smile in the tone. Present moment — she's with him now in the memory, not asking him to remember.
